gloss: wheat gluten; fu (dried or fresh gluten cake)

definitions.gloss: wheat gluten; fu (dried or fresh gluten cake)
definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese food made from wheat gluten, available in dried or fresh forms and used in soups, stews, and other dishes.

examples.japanese: {味噌汁|みそしる}に{麩|ふ}を{入|い}れる。
{乾燥|かんそう}した{麩|ふ}を{水|みず}で{戻|もど}す。
{京都|きょうと}の{生麩|なまふ}は{和菓子|わがし}にも{使|つか}われる。
examples.english: Fresh fu from Kyoto is also used in Japanese confections.

examples.japanese: {麩|ふ}は{低|てい}カロリーで{高|こう}たんぱくな{食材|しょくざい}として{見直|みなお}されている。
examples.english: Fu is being reconsidered as a low-calorie, high-protein ingredient.

notes:
A traditional Japanese ingredient made by washing wheat flour dough to extract the gluten. Comes in two main forms: {焼|や}き{麩|ふ} (baked and dried fu) and {生麩|なまふ} (fresh fu).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {焼|や}き{麩|ふ}: baked/dried fu — the most common type, light and spongy
- {生麩|なまふ}: fresh fu — a Kyoto specialty with a soft, mochi-like texture
- {車麩|くるまふ}: wheel-shaped fu — a large ring-shaped dried fu, specialty of Niigata
- {麩|ふ}の{味噌汁|みそしる}: miso soup with fu
- {麩菓子|ふがし}: fu snack — a sweet snack made from baked fu coated in brown sugar

SIMILAR WORDS:
- グルテン: gluten — the loanword, used in scientific or Western food contexts
- {豆腐|とうふ}: tofu — also a protein-rich traditional food, but made from soybeans rather than wheat

CULTURAL NOTE:
Fu has been a staple of Japanese Buddhist vegetarian cuisine ({精進料理|しょうじんりょうり}) for centuries. {生麩|なまふ} from Kyoto is considered a delicacy and is often shaped into decorative forms for use in traditional {懐石|かいせき} cuisine.
